The daily work of fence erectors revolves around the process of "layout—excavation—posts—mesh—gate": measure the fence line and mark post positions according to drawings or client requirements, and confirm there are no cables or water pipes in the work area before digging; dig post holes with shovels, post hole diggers or power augers; set metal or wooden posts vertically and correct plumb with a string line, plumb bob or level; pour concrete at the base or backfill and tamp into place; install rails and braces on the posts and saw lumber or cut metal pipe as needed; stretch wire, wire mesh or chain link fencing and fasten it to the frame; assemble fence gates and install them in place; also build and repair structures such as baffles, retaining walls and trellises; discuss fence needs with clients and estimate and quote; some work uses portable gas welding equipment to weld metal parts, and in special cases rock may be handled by blasting to allow post holes to be dug.

Work context｜Fence erectors work on outdoor sites in residential, ranch, municipal and construction settings, forming a construction cycle around layout and positioning, excavation and posts, foundation fixing, rails and mesh, and gates and accessories.

entries.answer: Build and repair fences and fence gates using hand and power tools: measure the fence line and mark post positions according to drawings, and confirm there are no cables or water pipes in the area before digging; dig post holes with shovels, post hole diggers or power augers and set metal or wooden posts vertically and correct plumb with a level and string line; pour concrete at the base or backfill and tamp into place; install rails and braces and saw lumber or cut metal pipe to make rails; stretch wire, wire mesh or chain link fencing and fasten it to the frame; assemble and install fence gates; also build and repair structures such as baffles, retaining walls and trellises; and discuss fence needs with clients and estimate and quote.
entries.question: What do fence erectors mainly do?

entries.answer: The objects of responsibility differ: this occupation mainly covers layout and positioning, post excavation, installation of rails and mesh, and assembly of fence gates; carpenters mainly make and fit out wooden structures; cement masons and concrete finishers mainly pour and finish concrete surfaces; construction laborers mainly do site cleaning, carrying and auxiliary work; drywall and ceiling tile installers mainly install indoor panels and ceilings; electricians are responsible for installing electrical wiring and equipment; landscaping and groundskeeping workers are responsible for planting and site upkeep; roofers mainly do roof waterproofing and tile laying; and first-line supervisors of construction trades are responsible for assigning tasks and supervising construction quality and safety.

entries.answer: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1–2 (little to some preparation), SVP below 6.0; in the education survey about 48% indicated that a high school diploma or equivalent is needed and 29% indicated below a high school diploma. Related occupational training usually requires a high school or GED credential, with pre-employment training ranging from a few days to one year. Special operations such as welding, excavation and work at height require training and the corresponding qualification according to local requirements; special operations such as blasting must follow special permit requirements. In mainland China, construction experience plus post training is commonly required, and the specifics are subject to recruitment announcements and local provisions.

entries.answer: A more accurate judgment is that some tasks will be assisted by tools and that the occupation as a whole will mainly see augmentation and structural adjustment. A 2023 ILO study shows that task exposure varies widely across occupations and that technical feasibility does not mean enterprises have already adopted it; meanwhile layout and positioning, post correction, excavation and work at height, and underground utility and geological judgment require on-site experience and responsibility, so the conclusion is that the way of working will change rather than that the occupation as a whole will be replaced.
entries.question: Will this occupation be replaced by AI?

entries.answer: No. The median is the midpoint of the wage distribution of practitioners within the same statistical period, not a starting salary. Schedules for this occupation are mainly fixed shifts with some seasonal work, and some work is priced per meter or per project; personal income must be judged together with the pay method (daily or hourly, per meter pricing or project lump sum) and actual hours (O*NET work context shows 89% of respondents work 40 hours per week, 11% more than 40 hours, and 27% seasonal work).

entries.answer: Yes. Related occupational training shows that pre-employment training for this occupation ranges from a few days to one year, and most posts are taken up through mentoring. However, posts involving welding, excavation and work at height usually require safety training and special qualifications; underground utility confirmation must be carried out according to utility owner and competent authority requirements. Whether it is feasible depends on the target employer and local provisions, and this page does not replace the original regulations and does not provide engineering or construction safety advice.
